findings.reason: split it into one node per cause, or the gate closes a single verdict over two mechanisms and proves neither.
findings.text: §48's Deliverable carries two independent changes — (a) at most one ledger load per view, with the live row's session resolved from the committed rows by run id, and (b) the path-derived fields computed only for the rows returned, after filtering, sorting and the limit — each with its own measure (the `ledger.load` count and the `_path_exists` count) and its own failure mode, so one node's verdict cannot say which half landed

findings.reason: the requirement needs per-project scoping plus either a workstation-scope arm or an explicit fence to project scope, otherwise the stated invariant and the gate disagree about what a correct implementation is and the hidden defect is a wrong session on a returned row.
findings.text: "One runs view makes at most one ledger load" and "The view reads the project's committed rows at most once" are stated for `runs_view` as a whole, but that view is also a multi-project reader: under `scope="workstation"` the ledger arm reads one ledger per mounted project (`reckon/crew/query.py:552-570`) and the live arm passes a per-row `checkout_path` from `_record_repository` (`reckon/crew/query.py:530-541`), so the invariant is false for any workstation view over more than one project; the done-when's fixture is a single project, so a worker honouring "at most one" literally by sharing one read across projects would resolve some live rows' `session_id` and `session_id_source` against another project's ledger, and the gate cannot see it
